P2.what: NCAA altitude table in core; parse SwimCloud 'A' tag. First capture a live swim carrying 'A' (try a Wyoming or Air Force swimmer) to learn whether eventtime is actual or adjusted.

evidence.fixture: tests/fixtures/profile_fastest_times-1401610-altitude.json (35 rows, saved 2026-09-22 via Orca embedded browser, same-origin fetch after Cloudflare cleared)
evidence.row: swimmer 1401610 (Simon Casey, Wyoming), 400 Free LCM, CSI Long Course Open (meet 386418, event 68), 2026-06-14, eventtime 247.11, flag "A", flags[{label:"A",title:"Altitude Adjusted"}], row id 180371296 but url ?id=179094351
evidence.actualTime: Meet results page /results/386418/event/68/ row for swim 179094351: "2 Simon Casey Wyoming Aquatics 4:12.11" = 252.11 s
evidence.conclusion: profile_fastest_times eventtime is the ALTITUDE-ADJUSTED time, not the swim. 252.11 - 247.11 = 5.00 = NCAA 400 m value for 4,251-6,500 ft. The actual time is NOT in the JSON; only the adjusted one. SwimCloud chose the elevation class; do not re-derive it.
implications: Do not apply the NCAA altitude table again to an A-tagged time (double adjustment).
Label A-tagged times as altitude-adjusted everywhere; the swum time is not available from this endpoint.
Apply the NCAA table only to times known to be swum at altitude and NOT already adjusted (e.g. PDF/manual imports with a known elevation).
